en.headline: Police to activate facial recognition on SmartView cameras from 16 November
en.dek: Commissioner Chow said the facial recognition function of the SmartView programme would start next Monday and described it as protection for law-abiding citizens.
body: Police Commissioner Joe Chow said the facial recognition capability under the SmartView closed-circuit television programme would be activated on 16 November.
Chow described the function as protection for good citizens and monitoring for those who commit crimes. He noted that the force had already explained the operational details earlier.

The programme has been running for about two years, with more than 10,000 cameras now installed across Hong Kong on lamp posts, smart lamp posts, government buildings and police vehicles. The force aims to reach 60,000 cameras by 2028.

Police are also in discussions with at least four shopping malls about connecting their cameras to the system, including Ocean Terminal, Tuen Mun Town Plaza, Kwai Chung Plaza and Ling Le Hu in Fanling.

zh.headline: 警方銳眼計劃下周一啟動人面識別功能
zh.dek: 警務處處長周一鳴表示，銳眼計劃的人面識別功能將於11月16日啟用，形容對良好市民屬保障，對作姦犯科者則屬監控。
body: 警務處處長周一鳴表示，警方「銳眼計劃」的人面識別功能將於下周一，即11月16日啟動。
周一鳴形容有關功能對良好市民屬保障，對作姦犯科的人則屬監控，並指警方早前已交代操作內容。
計劃實施約兩年，現時已安裝超過一萬支鏡頭，分布於一般燈柱、智慧燈柱、政府建築物及警車。警方目標於2028年將鏡頭總數增至六萬支。
警方正與至少四個商場洽商，將其閉路電視接入系統，包括奧海城、屯門市廣場、葵涌商場及粉嶺嶺·樂活。
